title: Today in one sentence
text: The market ended almost flat (SPY -0.1%, QQQ -0.7%), but money moved around: Meta (+3.4%) and Microsoft (+1.1%) went up, while chip and space companies like TSMC (-2.0%), AMD (-2.3%), NVIDIA (-1.3%) and Rocket Lab (-3.7%) went down.

title: Meta is close to its high
text: Meta rose 3.4% to $742.96. It is now about 5% below its highest price of the past year ($779.82) and about 5% below what experts expect it to be worth in a year ($781). When a stock gets close to the experts' guess, there is less room left in that guess.

title: AMD already sits near its target
text: AMD fell 2.3% to $594.24, but the experts' average guess is $607.59, only 2% higher. AMD is also a roller coaster stock (beta 2.5, which means it tends to move about two and a half times as much as the market), so its price can swing a lot in either direction.

title: Big inflation report on Wednesday
text: The September inflation report (how fast prices are rising) comes out Wednesday, Oct. 14. Experts expect prices to be up around 3.6% from a year ago, which would be higher than August's 3.4%. These are forecasts, not facts yet. The Fed meets Oct. 27 to 28, and higher inflation can keep interest rates high, which tends to hurt expensive stocks like AMD.

title: Lesson 3: What is a dividend?
text: A dividend is a small payment that some companies send to their owners, usually every three months, just for holding the stock. Think of it as a thank-you share of the profits. Microsoft and Lockheed Martin pay dividends, while Amazon, AMD and Rocket Lab do not, because they keep their money to grow. The fund SCHD is built from companies that pay steady dividends, which is why it has been a calmer ride (beta 0.58). A dividend is not free money: the stock price usually drops a little when the dividend is paid.

title: What we could and could not check
text: Prices are from the close on Oct. 12. Analyst targets and some company numbers are not available for Broadcom, Vertiv, Rocket Lab, Eli Lilly and Intuitive Surgical, and the ETFs have no targets, so those stay blank. News is picked by hand from public sources.
